source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Continuity, competence, trust, and authority are separate institutional questions that require distinct protocol objects, decision owners, and failure rules.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: This Article develops Persona Protocol as a proposed trust-continuity layer for autonomous systems. The protocol separates four questions that current designs collapse. Continuity asks whether the present actor is the same governed Persona that earned a record. Competence asks what that Persona has demonstrated in a defined domain and context. Trust asks what confidence a relying party may place in that evidence for a specific decision. Authority asks whether an authorized principal has granted permission for the proposed action under current policy limits. These four questions require distinct protocol objects, distinct decision owners, and distinct failure rules.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Reputation continuity is a transaction-cost, credible-commitment, and monitoring problem before it is an engineering problem.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Reputation continuity is a transaction-cost problem, a credible-commitment problem, and a monitoring problem before it is an engineering problem.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol represents reputation as a contextual projection over provenance-bearing evidence, preserves adverse lifecycle states, permits selective principal disclosure, and treats authority as an explicit, scoped, revocable grant that fails closed.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol therefore represents reputation as a contextual projection over provenance-bearing evidence rather than as a transferable scalar. It preserves adverse, withheld, challenged, revoked, and superseded events. It permits selective principal disclosure. It treats authority as an explicit, scoped, revocable grant that fails closed.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol proposes a minimum separation of trust functions for autonomous actors that may be persistent without public identification, competent without authorization, and trusted for one decision without being trusted for all decisions.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The contribution is institutional and architectural. Persona Protocol proposes a minimum separation of trust functions for a world in which autonomous actors are persistent without being publicly identified, competent without being authorized, and trusted for one decision without being trusted for all decisions.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Continuity, competence, trust, and authority are four institutional determinations with four different owners, not four formulations of one identity question.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: These are not four phrasings of one identity question. They are four institutional determinations with four different owners.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: An identifier-key binding does not determine legitimate reputation inheritance, a credential does not determine cross-domain weight, a reputation score does not create present authority, and an authority grant does not establish competence.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The distinction matters because autonomous systems move across runtimes, replace keys, change models, decompose into subagents, and operate under delegated authority. A conventional account binds an identifier to a key. It cannot, without additional governance, determine whether the current system legitimately inherits the reputation of an earlier system. A credential states a fact. It does not fix the weight of that fact in a new domain. A reputation score summarizes prior observations. It does not create present authority. A valid authority grant permits an action. It does not establish that the grantee is competent.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Collapsing identity, reputation, trust, and authority into one score or token hides institutional judgment inside a scoring rule and ownership record rather than eliminating it.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Design by collapse remains design. When identity, reputation, trust, and authority merge into one score or one token, the resulting system does not eliminate institutional judgment. It hides the judgment inside a scoring rule and an ownership record.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol is a continuity and evidence architecture, not a universal identity system, final reputation algorithm, or authority provider.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: This Article develops Persona Protocol as a proposed alternative. The protocol is not a new universal identity system. It is not a final reputation algorithm. It is not an authority provider. It is a continuity and evidence architecture that makes reputation claims inspectable, contextual, contestable, and portable while preserving the separation between operational state, principal identity, risk judgment, and authority allocation.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Portable trust continuity is legitimate only when every contribution traces to evidence, validation, governance, context, challenge state, and time.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The central claim is bounded. Autonomous systems require portable trust continuity, but portable trust continuity is legitimate only when every contribution traces to evidence, validation, governance, context, challenge state, and time.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Cross-organizational autonomous-agent transactions face screening, verification, and credible-commitment costs that can force counterparties to absorb risk, reject external agents, or require human guarantors.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Applied to autonomous systems, the framework yields a specific diagnosis. An autonomous agent transacting across an organizational boundary faces high ex ante screening costs, high ex post verification costs, and almost no credible commitment technology. It cannot post a bond. It cannot be sued in its own name. It cannot be reliably excluded from re-entry. Its counterparty therefore either absorbs the risk, collapses the relationship into a hierarchy by refusing all external agents, or demands a human guarantor and thereby forfeits the coordination gain the agent was supposed to deliver.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A reputation history can substitute for a bond only if it attaches to a subject that cannot costlessly shed it, is interpretable in the present domain, and is contestable and inspectable.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: A reputation history is the missing safeguard. It substitutes for the bond by making adverse conduct costly to the actor rather than only to the counterparty. But a reputation history performs that function only under three conditions. The history must attach to an accountable subject that cannot costlessly shed it. The history must be interpretable in the domain of the present transaction. The history must be contestable by the subject and inspectable by the relying party.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The institutional deficit in agent trust concerns the governed objects that signatures carry, not the availability of cryptographic signatures themselves.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: That is the institutional deficit. It is not a gap in cryptography. Signatures are solved. It is a gap in the institutional objects that signatures are asked to carry.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Eliminating psychological guile does not eliminate objective misalignment: a faithfully optimizing agent can impose counterparty losses without deception, and verifiability alone does not determine whether to transact.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Second, the elimination of psychological guile does not eliminate misalignment. An agent with a faithfully executed objective function can still impose losses on a counterparty whose objective differs. Opportunism in the Williamsonian sense is self-interest seeking with guile; an agent optimizing a specified objective against a counterparty's interest produces the same institutional harm without the guile. Verifiability tells a relying party what the agent did. It does not tell the relying party whether to transact.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: When generative output is abundant but validation capacity remains scarce, allocating validation attention across abundant claimants becomes more important rather than less.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Validation capacity is governance capacity. If governance capacity remains scarce while generative output becomes abundant, then the allocation of scarce validation attention across abundant claimants is precisely the problem a reputation architecture exists to solve, and it becomes more acute rather than less.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Control of a current key does not establish the truth of a signed claim, supply a legitimate reputation function, or determine whether a material system change preserves the accountable subject.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: That generality is a strength. It also defines the boundary. Control of a current key does not establish the truth of a signed claim. A credential does not itself supply a legitimate reputation function. Neither determines whether a material model or controller change preserves the accountable subject that earned a record.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol composes with identity and credential standards but adds the distinct object of governed continuity for a reputation-bearing history.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol composes with identity and credential standards. It does not replace them. Its distinct object is governed continuity of a reputation-bearing history.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Reputation should be represented as an evidence set, expertise graph, validation record, and purpose-bound projection rather than as a universal score.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The proper representation is therefore not a universal score. It is an evidence set, an expertise graph, a validation record, and a purpose-bound projection.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Trust may inform risk, but only an authorized issuer can create authority; reputation may satisfy a grant condition but cannot substitute for or enlarge the grant.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol adopts a strong separation rule. Trust may inform risk. Only an authorized issuer may create authority. A high reputation projection can satisfy a condition inside a grant. It cannot substitute for the grant. Historical responsibility can inform a relying party. It cannot enlarge the present action, resource, amount, duration, or delegation depth.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A system that converts reputation directly into authority gives the author of the projection rule control over the action allocation.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The distinction is institutional, not semantic. Whoever converts reputation directly into authority controls the action surface through the scoring rule. Whoever writes the projection then writes the allocation.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Operational telemetry can become evidence, but task counts, uptime, registrations, messages, executions, and state transitions are not reputation merely because they exist.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Agent systems generate abundant telemetry: task counts, uptime, registrations, messages, executions, and state transitions. These records can become evidence. They are not reputation merely because they exist.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Externally eligible reputation requires an intervening governed admission decision recorded in an evidence event that identifies artifact, context, mode, taxonomy, validator set, governance rule, outcome, time, and content commitment.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol therefore requires an intervening governed admission decision. An evidence event identifies the artifact, context, mode, taxonomy, validator set, governance rule, outcome, time, and content commitment.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Synthetic fixtures, operator canaries, directory listings, and repeated raw observations do not become externally eligible reputation without governed validation.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Synthetic fixtures remain synthetic. Operator canaries remain operator activity. Registry listings remain discoverability. Raw observations do not become validated claims through repetition.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol does not eliminate Sybil corruption; its narrower claim is to make the cost of corruption legible.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol does not falsify it either. The protocol's claim is narrower: it makes the cost of corruption legible rather than eliminating it.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol versions and publishes projection profiles and permits competing profiles over a shared evidence commitment so that scoring rules remain revisable.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol therefore versions the projection profile, publishes it, and permits competing profiles over a shared evidence commitment.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol supplies portability and continuity but does not itself supply calibrated slashing, robust Sybil resistance, or maintained human oversight.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The scope concession. The path from engineered consequence to reliable agent conduct "is not guaranteed," and depends on correct institutional design at each phase, including appropriate slashing parameters, robust Sybil resistance, calibrated reputation portability, and maintained human oversight (Kaal 2026b, claim 6244278-039). Persona Protocol supplies the portability and continuity layer. It supplies none of the other three.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A Persona is a persistent protocol subject that accumulates a continuity-bound evidence history and need not correspond to a human, model, runtime, wallet, organization, or public principal.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: A Persona is a persistent protocol subject that accumulates a continuity-bound evidence history. It may correspond to one agent, a governed ensemble, or another autonomous system. It is not necessarily a human, model, runtime, wallet, organization, or public principal.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A Persona may survive governed rotation, migration, recovery, or declared upgrades, but material changes must produce a continuity event, fork, or new Persona, and principal disclosure remains policy-dependent.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The answer may survive key rotation, runtime migration, recovery, or a declared model upgrade. It must not survive silently. Material changes require a continuity event, a fork, or a new Persona under the applicable governance rule. Principal disclosure remains policy-dependent. A regulated transaction may require it. A low-risk scholarly contribution may not.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona evaluation uses four sequential, fail-closed gates, and a later gate cannot satisfy an earlier gate.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Separation of functions is meaningful only if it produces an ordered procedure. Persona Protocol specifies four sequential gates, each of which fails closed and none of which may be satisfied by a later gate.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: An unverifiable continuity link terminates reputation inheritance at that point, so evidence earned before the unverifiable transition does not transfer forward.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: First, continuity. The verifier resolves the Persona document, walks the continuity log to the record's origin, and confirms that every transition satisfied the governance rule in force at the time of the transition. An unverifiable link terminates the inheritance at that point. Evidence earned before an unverifiable transition does not transfer forward.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Evidence sufficiency is evaluated within the relevant domain, mode, and time window, and coverage must be read before any aggregate.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Second, evidence sufficiency. The relying party filters admitted evidence to the domain, mode, and time window relevant to the present decision, and reads coverage before reading any aggregate. Sparse coverage is a finding, not a defect in the display.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A contextual projection and its uncertainty are inputs to a risk decision, not the decision itself.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Third, projection. The relying party applies a declared projection profile to the filtered evidence and obtains a contextual value together with its uncertainty and its input commitment. The value is an input to a risk decision. It is not the decision.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Authority must be verified independently of continuity, evidence sufficiency, and trust projection, with denial unless every required grant element verifies.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Fourth, authority. The evaluator verifies the grant chain independently of the first three gates and denies unless every required element verifies.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Evidence events are immutable, signed, content-addressed, and append-only; corrections supersede rather than erase, and adverse lifecycle states remain in history.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: An evidence event is immutable, signed, content-addressed, and append-only. Corrections create superseding events. Rejections, withholdings, challenges, revocations, and overturned decisions remain part of the history.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Validator independence must be demonstrated through disclosed operators, datasets, incentives, and governance structures rather than inferred from distinct validator names.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Independence must be demonstrated, not assumed. Missing attestations do not become agreement. Multiple validators do not become independent merely because their names differ. Shared operators, datasets, incentives, or governance structures must be disclosed and reflected in a projection profile.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Projection profiles must disclose whether consensus strength affects evidence weight and may use loosely coupled admission for contested categories to avoid suppressing minority evaluation.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol therefore requires that a profile disclose whether it treats consensus strength as evidence weight, and permits loosely coupled admission for contested categories.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The founding validator assumption must be recorded with its governance basis so relying parties can discount the subtree that descends from it.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The first validator in any admission system is admitted by assertion rather than by evidence. Persona Protocol requires that the assertion be recorded as such, with its governance basis, so that a later relying party can discount the entire subtree that descends from it.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Multiple admission systems may export a common minimum receipt while retaining their local rules.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The design permits multiple admission systems to export a common minimum receipt while retaining local rules.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Expertise is represented through a versioned directed graph in which historical evidence retains its original tag and taxonomy version, and later mappings cannot rewrite source events.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Competence is multidimensional. Persona Protocol represents expertise through a versioned directed graph. Tags may be added, deprecated, aliased, split, or merged. Historical evidence retains its original tag and its taxonomy version. Mapping records may support later projections. They cannot rewrite the source event.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Graph adjacency does not prove competence transfer, local stages do not create universal rank, and cross-system comparison requires a declared, fallible crosswalk.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Horizontal and vertical development are graph views, not automatic promotions. Adjacency between fields does not prove transfer. A stage inside one admission system does not become a universal rank. Cross-system comparison requires a declared crosswalk, and a crosswalk is a claim that can be wrong.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A derivation edge is evidence about both contributing Personas, and its dispute path must be declared in advance.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol treats a derivation edge as evidence about both Personas, and requires that the dispute path for a contested edge be declared in advance

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Agent Reputation Identity is a versioned contextual projection over a committed evidence set, not a universal identity.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Agent Reputation Identity, or ARI, is a versioned contextual projection over a committed evidence set. The label is retained for the projection mechanism, not for a universal identity.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A conforming projection discloses its filters, taxonomy mapping, validator and outcome treatment, decay, uncertainty, weights, aggregation, eligibility, rounding, expertise vector, and coverage.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: A conforming projection identifies its input filters, taxonomy mapping, validator treatment, outcome treatment, decay, uncertainty, weights, aggregation, eligibility rules, and rounding. It exposes the expertise vector and the coverage behind any aggregate. Corrected evidence changes a later projection without deleting history.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Evidence commitments should be portable across competing projection profiles because a single canonical scoring rule gives its controller unrecorded allocative authority.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Evidence is shared; projections compete. A single canonical scoring rule reconstitutes precisely the centralized authority the architecture is meant to avoid, because the entity that controls the rule controls the allocation without ever appearing in the authority path.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Projection-profile authorship belongs with the evaluated domain rather than with a central specification body.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The corollary is that profile authorship belongs with the domain rather than with the specification body.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The reference projection formula is an uncalibrated engineering demonstration and must not be treated as a validated production measure.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The reference profile weights positive and negative evidence mass within a rated domain. That formula is an engineering demonstration. It has not been empirically calibrated. No production decision should treat its numerical output as a validated measure.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Missing evidence is null rather than zero; below a declared domain coverage threshold, a projection reports coverage and uncertainty without an aggregate.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The first rule is that missing evidence is null, not zero. A domain in which a Persona has no admitted evidence yields no value. It does not yield a neutral value, and it does not yield a low value. The reference profile's neutral baseline applies only after a declared minimum coverage threshold is met within the rated domain. Below that threshold the projection returns coverage and uncertainty without an aggregate. A baseline applied to an empty domain is a fabricated prior wearing the costume of a measurement.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Governed continuity and explicit coverage relocate the newcomer penalty into a legible, domain-scoped cost that can be discharged through evidence, but they do not abolish entry cost.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Because continuity is governed and adverse events are preserved, the cost of abandoning a history is borne by the abandoning actor rather than distributed across all counterparties. Because coverage is explicit, the penalty a newcomer faces is legible, domain-scoped, and dischargeable through evidence. The protocol converts an implicit and unbounded suspicion into an explicit and dischargeable one. It does not abolish the entry cost

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Every continuity event links to its predecessor and identifies the governance policy in force before the transition.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Continuity events include creation, key rotation, verification-method change, runtime migration, material upgrade, fork, recovery, compromise, suspension, and deactivation. Each event links to the prior event and identifies the policy in force before the transition.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Key transfer alone does not transfer reputation; forks require allocation rules, mergers cannot silently sum scores, and recovery cannot erase a compromised interval.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Key transfer alone does not transfer reputation. A fork cannot clone a full record into multiple descendants without declared allocation rules. A merger cannot silently sum scores. Recovery cannot erase the compromised interval.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol cannot prevent out-of-band control sales, but observable changes in keys, verification methods, or governing principals must produce continuity events that relying parties can use to discount inherited evidence.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: It does not attempt to prevent an out-of-band sale of control, which no protocol can prevent. It requires that any change in the controlling key, verification method, or governing principal produce a continuity event that is visible to every downstream relying party, and it permits a relying party to discount or disregard all evidence earned before any transition it regards as a substitution of the accountable subject.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Trust relationships require typed, directed, scoped, sourced, and time-bounded edges because scalar representations destroy relationship information.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Relationships among Personas, validators, artifacts, principals, organizations, governance bodies, and expertise tags carry information that a scalar destroys. Persona Protocol uses typed, directed, scoped, sourced, and time-bounded edges.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Validation, collaboration, membership, recognition, and authority are distinct relations, and circular graph paths do not establish independent support.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Validation is not delegation. Collaboration is not endorsement. Membership is not competence. Recognition is not authority. Circular paths do not prove independent support.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Trust-graph algorithms must disclose path rules, cycle treatment, correlation assumptions, and centrality effects because a trust graph is a provenance structure before it is a scoring structure.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Graph algorithms must disclose path rules, cycle treatment, correlation assumptions, and centrality effects. A trust graph is a provenance structure before it is a scoring structure.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Authority grants must identify issuer, subject, action, resource, constraints, time, delegation depth, revocation, policy, and proof; child grants may preserve or narrow but never enlarge scope.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: An authority grant identifies the issuer, the subject Persona, the action, the resource, the constraints, the validity period, the delegation depth, the revocation status, the governing policy, and the proof. A child grant may narrow or preserve scope. It may not enlarge amount, duration, action, resource, disclosure rights, or delegation depth.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Authority evaluation denies by default when required grant elements cannot be verified, and a reputation projection may be a grant condition but cannot become the grant.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The authority evaluator denies by default when continuity, grant validity, scope, time, limits, revocation status, or mandatory policy cannot be verified. A projection may appear as one risk condition inside a grant. It does not become the grant.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Public Persona data should be minimal, with principal identity, raw artifacts, model internals, customer data, validator deliberations, recovery contacts, and protected attributes restricted by default.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Public Persona data should be minimal. Principal identity, raw work artifacts, model internals, customer data, validator deliberations, recovery contacts, and protected attributes remain restricted by default.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A Persona record should be owned by its subject rather than its host, while append-only integrity should be reconciled with privacy through tombstones, encryption, restricted stores, and selective disclosure.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Two constraints follow. First, the record must be owned by its subject rather than by a host. On centralized platforms, "users earned their reputation but do NOT own reputation," and an account deletion destroys years of history with "near zero ability to reclaim the data," while scores remain "trapped in Silos" with no path to aggregation across platforms (Calcaterra, Kaal, and Sivalingam 2018, claims 3266953-009 and 3266953-010). Portability of the evidence commitment is the remedy. Second, append-only integrity does not justify indefinite public exposure. Tombstones, encryption, restricted stores, and selective disclosure preserve accountability without making sensitive content universally public.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Continuity reduces whitewashing while creating persistent linkage risk, so the protocol manages rather than resolves the tension between accountability and privacy.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The residual risk is real and is not resolved. The same continuity guarantee that prevents whitewashing creates a persistent linkage surface, and distributed operation makes lawful data handling harder to demonstrate rather than easier: distribution "complicates the tracking of data flows and the enforcement of privacy controls, making it difficult to demonstrate compliance during audits" (Kaal 2024b, claim 4941807-027). The protocol manages this tension. It does not dissolve it.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Integration with MCP, A2A, credentials, attestations, and authority tokens does not change their evidentiary meaning: discovery is not competence, attestation is bounded by appraisal policy, credentials remain issuer claims, and authority remains issuer- and scope-bounded.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: None of these integrations changes the meaning of a protocol object. An MCP tool listing is not evidence of competence. An A2A Agent Card is a discovery and presentation document, even when signed. An attestation establishes only what its evidence and its appraisal policy support. A credential remains an issuer claim. An authority token remains bounded by its issuer and its scope.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol makes the reputation-bearing subject non-transferable by default and requires declared, visible continuity events for transitions, allowing relying parties to discount pre-transition evidence.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The reputation-bearing subject is non-transferable by default; transfer requires a declared continuity event that is visible to every downstream relying party and that permits the relying party to discount everything earned before the transition.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol offers a provisional constructive separation of functions that adjacent standards can implement, transport, or reference, without asserting a completed novelty review.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: That differentiation is provisional. A complete prior-art and standards review remains required before any strong novelty claim. The appropriate claim is constructive: Persona Protocol specifies one coherent separation of functions that adjacent standards can implement, transport, or reference, and it identifies one design choice in the adjacent literature that it regards as an error.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Passing the reference implementation's synthetic tests does not establish external validation, security, production readiness, calibrated projections, or independent interoperability.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: These are implementation facts, not external validation. The reference slice has no production network listener, durable database, production signature system, secure key store, transparency service, distributed consensus, real valve adapter, independently calibrated projection, or second implementation. Its fixtures are synthetic and externally ineligible. Passing tests is not a security audit.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The separation thesis is falsified if deployed systems routinely collapse the four gates into one score without reducing decision quality.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The separation thesis fails if relying parties in deployment routinely collapse the four gates into a single composite score without loss of decision quality, which would indicate that the separation imposes cost without informational benefit.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The non-transferability thesis is falsified if governed transfer with full disclosure produces the same downstream error rates as non-transferability.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The non-transferability thesis fails if governed transfer with full disclosure produces the same downstream error rates as non-transferability, which would indicate that disclosure alone is sufficient and the default is unnecessary.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The coverage thesis is falsified if suppressing aggregates below a coverage threshold produces worse relying-party outcomes than reporting a baseline.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The coverage thesis fails if projections that suppress aggregates below a coverage threshold produce worse relying-party outcomes than projections that report a baseline, which would indicate that a fabricated prior outperforms an honest silence.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The competing-profiles thesis is falsified if plural profiles over a shared evidence commitment converge to a de facto canonical rule in ordinary use.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The competing-profiles thesis fails if, over a shared evidence commitment, plural profiles converge to a de facto canonical rule in ordinary use, which would indicate that profile competition is nominal and that the Folk Theorem exposure has not in fact been mitigated.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol supplies an auditability condition for reputation governance but does not supply the metric-quality condition required for reliable outcomes.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol supplies the auditability condition. It does not supply the metric-quality condition, which remains local to each admission system.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Protocol governance must separate specification stewardship, evidence adjudication, and local authority; changes require documented analysis, and emergency powers must be narrow, temporary, logged, and reviewed.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The protocol requires bounded governance that separates specification stewardship, evidence adjudication, and local authority. Version changes require rationale, compatibility analysis, review, and security and privacy assessment. Emergency powers must be narrow, time-limited, logged, and reviewed.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A stable protocol release requires an open conformance suite and at least two independent interoperable implementations; no vendor implementation is itself the standard.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: No vendor implementation is the standard. A stable release claim requires an open conformance suite and at least two independent interoperable implementations.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Projection profiles should be openly published and selected locally by relying parties because a specification body that controls both evidence schema and canonical scoring holds unrecorded allocative power.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Governance of the projection profile deserves separate treatment because it is the locus of capture. A specification body that controls both the evidence schema and the canonical scoring rule holds allocative power that no authority grant records. The failure pattern is well documented: recentralization is the central obstacle to decentralized governance of AI systems (Kaal 2024a, claim 4796714-012), and consensus mechanisms that weight power by holdings "centralize control based on the quantity of tokens held, potentially skewing governance in favor of the wealthy" (Kaal 2024a, claim 4796714-014). Persona Protocol therefore treats profile publication as open and profile selection as local to the relying party.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Reputation governance must be revisable on the timescale of exploitation and able to ingest evidence of its own gaming.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Governance must also be revisable on the timescale of the exploit rather than the timescale of the standards cycle. The Folk Theorem result forecloses a static rule set. The author's dynamic-regulation framework supplies the alternative: rules are adaptable only where "the institutions and rulemaking processes that produce them integrate dynamic elements that generate timely, relevant, and decentralized information for rulemaking" (Kaal 2013, claim 2267560-012). A reputation protocol whose governance cannot ingest evidence of its own gaming is a reputation protocol with a fixed expiry date.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol's principal threat model includes seizure, whitewashing, reputation purchase, synthetic-evidence laundering, collusion, bootstrap capture, replay, graph rings, taxonomy gaming, projection manipulation, authority escalation, deanonymization, stale projections, and governance capture.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The principal threats are Persona seizure, reputation whitewashing, reputation purchase, synthetic-evidence laundering, collusive validation, validator bootstrapping capture, replay, graph rings, taxonomy gaming, projection-profile manipulation, authority escalation, deanonymization, stale projections, and governance capture.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Persona Protocol does not claim to solve its threat model; implementations must identify the control, residual risk, and decision boundary for each threat.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Persona Protocol does not claim to solve these threats. It requires that implementations identify the control, the residual risk, and the decision boundary for each.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: The Trust Capital hypothesis predicts that sustained, independently validated, portable reputation may reduce transactional uncertainty and lower contracting costs across organizational boundaries.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: The economic hypothesis is Trust Capital: sustained, independently validated, portable reputation may reduce uncertainty in future transactions and thereby lower the cost of contracting across organizational boundaries. The hypothesis has a direct antecedent in the author's work on reputation functioning as capital in decentralized allocation (Kaal 2023) and on reputation as the governance substrate for AI systems (Kaal 2024b). The mechanism by which reputation substitutes for redundancy is already specified: where a high-reputation participant completes a task, required duplication can fall substantially, and that substitution is what permits work to scale (Kaal 2024d, claim 4734750-036).

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Trust Capital is capital in an institutional sense rather than a balance-sheet sense.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Trust Capital is therefore capital in the institutional sense, not in the balance-sheet sense.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: Testing Trust Capital requires causal evidence linking defined reputation histories to transaction terms, collateral, loss, selection, or authority decisions; until then it remains a hypothesis rather than an asset or price.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Establishing the hypothesis requires causal evidence connecting defined reputation histories to transaction terms, collateral, loss, selection, or authority decisions. Until that evidence exists, Trust Capital remains a hypothesis, not an asset, a token, a price, or a balance-sheet item.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems

claim: A protocol can preserve evidence of a reputation decision but cannot by itself supply the decision's lawfulness or legitimacy.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: A protocol can preserve the evidence of a decision. It cannot supply the lawfulness or the legitimacy of the decision by itself.
